main_text.l: collocet. Quod si fiduciam in Diabolo & men-
dacio collocet, necesse est pereuntibus iis qui-
bus nititur, & ipsum una dispereat.
Acquieverunt] Verbum Græcum significat, sibi
placuerunt. hoc fidei consequens est acquiescere
in re quæ fide apprehensa est: cum autem ac-
quiescit cor hominis in mendacio & vanitate, in
qua nihil est solidi, id plane arguit, cor [?ἀναίσθητον]
omnis sensus expers esse; estque hæc pœna quæ
cordi justo Dei judicio infligitur, cum omnis
sensus ipsi eripitur; quemadmodū pœna men-
tis, uti diximus, est deceptio & excæcatio. Ex-
cæcatā jam mente & tradito homine in men-
tem omnis judicii expertem, justo Dei judicio
punitur cor istā omnis veri sensus privatione;
quia per duritiem cordis eam, qua restitit veri-ta-
ti Dei, factum est ut mens excæcaretur: pœnam
igitur mentis justo Dei judicio sequitur pœna
cordis, hæc nimirum, qua dum fluctuat & eva-
nescit cum vanitate ea qua nititur, putat tamen
sese quiescere & in solido aliquo con-sistere fun-
damento.

l.i: 13 Nos autem debemus gratias agere Deo semper de
vobis, fratres dilecti a Domino, quod elegerit vos Deus ab
initio ad salutem per sanctificationem Spiritus, & fidem
14 Quò vocavit vos per Evangelium nostrum, ad ob-
tinendam gloriam Domini nostri Jesu Christi.

page.notes: The Greek word after "cor" is printed in Greek letters and is only partly legible at this scan resolution; it is marked [?]. "Quò" in verse 14 carries a mark over the ò that I read as a tilde-like accent. "istā" carries a macron on the a, read as an abbreviation for istam; the printed form is kept. The long s in "Deofemper", "fenfus", "fententiæ" and similar words is read as a plain s. The printed hyphens at line ends (qui-, men-, veri-ta-, eva-, con-, fun-, Ex-) are kept as printed. The word after "ad-" is on the next page and is not visible here, so no catchword is given.
